stops.note: wormwood, the bitter herb used to flavor the potent green spirit

settled in French for the strong, anise-flavored spirit made with wormwood; the spirit was first distilled in Switzerland's Val-de-Travers in the late 1700s, and French soldiers dosed with it in Algeria in the 1840s brought the habit home
the drink became notorious in Paris café culture and was banned in France in 1915
stops.meaning: a potent green liqueur flavored with wormwood and anise

current_meaning: a strong green liqueur flavored with wormwood and anise
